steps: Blend the pitted dates with the pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds in a food processor until the mixture starts to clump.
Add the cocoa powder and a pinch of salt and pulse until evenly combined and sticky.
Roll the mixture into 12 small balls, about 15g each.
Chill in the fridge for at least 20 minutes to firm up before serving.
Preheat the oven to 160C (140C fan) and line a small baking tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter, golden syrup and brown sugar together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Remove from the heat and stir in the rolled oats until fully coated.
Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the tin.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars.
Blend the dates and walnuts in a food processor until finely chopped and sticky.
Add the grated carrot, shredded coconut and a pinch of cinnamon and pulse until the mixture holds together.
Roll into 12 small balls.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.
Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and line a small baking tray with baking paper.
Soak the dried figs in a little hot water for 10 minutes, then blend with the honey to a smooth paste.
Mix the whole-wheat flour with a splash of water to form a soft dough.
Roll the dough out thin, spread with the fig paste, and roll up into a log.
Slice into 8 pieces and place on the tray.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until lightly golden, then cool before serving.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper muffin cups.
Combine the almond meal, oats, nuts, raisins, cinnamon, nutmeg, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Mix together the eggs, carrot, butter, maple syrup, and vanilla in a separate bowl.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing until just combined.
Spoon the batter into the muffin cups, filling each to the brim.
Bake until the muffins are nicely browned on top and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean, about 25 to 35 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper cases.
Mash the banana and beat with the eggs, peanut butter and honey until smooth.
Fold in the whole-wheat flour and baking soda until just combined.
Stir through the chocolate chips.
Divide the batter between the 12 muffin cases.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper cases.
Make the flax egg by mixing ground flaxseed with water and leaving for 5 minutes to gel.
Whisk the pumpkin purée, maple syrup, oat milk and flax egg together until smooth.
Fold in the oat flour, baking soda and pumpkin spice until just combined.
Divide the batter between the muffin cases.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Melt the coconut oil and stir in the maple syrup.
Mix in the rolled oats and whole-wheat flour until a thick dough forms.
Fold through the chocolate chips.
Scoop into 12 mounds on the tray and flatten slightly.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until golden at the edges, then cool on the tray.
Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg with the melted coconut oil and honey until smooth.
Stir in the almond flour until a soft dough forms.
Fold through the chocolate chips.
Scoop into 12 small mounds on the tray, flattening each slightly.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden at the edges, then cool on the tray before serving.
Preheat the oven to 190C (170C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mash the sweet potato with the black beans, cumin and a pinch of salt until combined.
Roll out the pie dough and cut into 8 rounds.
Spoon the filling onto one half of each round, fold over and crimp the edges to seal.
Place on the tray and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool for a few minutes before serving.
Rinse the baby potatoes and place in a pan of cold, salted water.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 15-20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and return to the pan.
Toss with the olive oil and salt while still warm.
Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Prick the sweet potato a few times with a fork and place on a baking tray.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until soft all the way through.
Split open and top with the coconut oil and cinnamon.
Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Pat the chickpeas dry with a towel and toss with the olive oil, smoked paprika and salt.
Spread in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Cool for a few minutes before serving; they crisp further as they cool.
Warm the tortilla briefly in a dry pan or microwave to make it pliable.
Spread the hummus evenly over the tortilla.
Scatter the spinach leaves over the hummus.
Top with the roasted sweet potato.
Roll the tortilla tightly, tucking in the sides, and slice in half to serve.
